record.title: AI fire alert precedes the first 911 call near Grass Valley
record.date_precision: Day and local alert time explicitly reported.
record.location: Near Grass Valley, California, United States
record.system: ALERTCalifornia camera network and DigitalPath/CAL FIRE fire-detection AI.
record.observed_outcome: AI alerted at 5:19 a.m. Firefighters were on scene before the first 911 call at 6:01 a.m. The fire remained under a quarter acre.
record.ai_contribution: Detected a possible ignition in the Wolf Mountain 1 camera feed and alerted firefighters.
record.human_contribution: The program uses trained watchstanders to confirm detections. Firefighters responded and contained this fire.
record.evidence_type: First-party program report. No independent causal evaluation.
record.evidence_supports: The university operating the camera program reports the alert, first-call times, and final containment.
record.limitations: Earlier notification and containment are observed. A larger fire, specific losses, or casualties avoided are not established. The comparison is with the first 911 call, not every possible detection route.
record.tradeoffs: No event-specific adverse effects are reported. False alarms, response costs, and surveillance effects are not evaluated.
record.replication_hypothesis: Test whether camera coverage, human confirmation, reliable dispatch, and available crews produce earlier effective responses elsewhere.
record.beneficiaries: Emergency responders received earlier notification. Nearby residents and property were intended downstream beneficiaries, but specific losses avoided are unmeasured.
